claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has an FCC/B2 dual-phase lamellar structure.
The FCC regions are enriched in Co, Cr, and Fe, whereas the B2 regions are enriched in Al and Ni.
Coupled eutectic growth produces an in-situ composite with high strength and ductility in the as-cast alloy.
The FCC matrix is chemically disordered in the as-cast state and lacks the relevant L12 ordering.
Aging near 600°C forms near-stoichiometric L12-ordered Ni3Al domains within the FCC matrix.
Near-stoichiometric L12 ordering in the FCC matrix produces a high antiphase-boundary energy.
Chemical short-range order can require additional energy for dislocation glide by creating diffuse antiphase boundaries.
Jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries develop or are present in the brittle 600°C-aged condition.
High APBE and jagged B2/FCC boundaries inhibit screw-dislocation cross-slip.
Cross-slip can create jogs that lock screw dislocations and require additional stress or thermal activation for unlocking.
Restricted cross-slip forces planar slip in the 600°C-aged alloy.
Planar slip bands concentrate stress where they terminate at serrations of jagged phase boundaries, initiating brittle fracture.
At approximately 750°C or above, the L12 order parameter and APBE decrease.
Aging near 750°C smooths the phase boundaries or forms ductile transition zones along them.
Reduced ordering at the higher aging temperature restores cross-slip and ductility.
The 600°C-aged material will have elongation below 5%, whereas the 750°C-aged material will have elongation above 15%.
The fracture mode changes from brittle fracture at 600°C to ductile dimple fracture at 750°C.
The 600°C-aged state will exhibit higher nanoindentation hardness and fewer pop-in events than the 750°C-aged state.
The brittle transition occurs when APBE exceeds the energy barrier for cross-slip.
The critical chemical boundary is reached when the local Ni/Al ratio in the FCC matrix approaches 3:1.

contradictions.description: The reversal is variously assigned to temperatures greater than 750°C and to aging at approximately or exactly 750°C, leaving the stated transition temperature internally inconsistent.
